About us · Women & Children Charity in Lagos

Every child deserves to feel included.

At the Sanusi Jafar Foundation, a non-profit for women and children, we believe some of the most important things we can give a person are not things at all.

They are

  • Hope.
  • Belonging.
  • Dignity.
  • The feeling of being seen.

Our work began with a simple belief:

Where a child comes from should never determine the kind of childhood they get to experience.

Where it started

Long before the Sanusi Jafar Foundation had a name, there was a childhood memory.

I remember a time when my uncle dressed up as Santa and gave gifts to children in our neighbourhood.

For some of us, it was simply the excitement of seeing Santa. The anticipation, the laughter and the magic of receiving a gift.

But I also remember seeing children around my age who experienced Father Christmas differently.

To them, Santa was almost a mirage something they could see, but never quite imagine experiencing for themselves.

It seemed like an experience reserved for children in private schools, privileged families or more affluent communities.

Even as a child, I remember thinking:

Why should that experience belong to some children and not others?

I remember wanting to become Santa myself.

Not because of the costume or the gifts, but because I wanted those children to experience what I had experienced.

I wanted them to know that they were not left out.

Because childhood memories stay with us.

Years later, we may forget the exact gift we received, but we remember how someone made us feel.

  • We remember being included.
  • We remember being celebrated.
  • We remember that, for a moment, the world made room for us.

That childhood thought stayed with me.

And years later, it became part of the reason the Sanusi Jafar Foundation exists.

Who we are

The Sanusi Jafar Foundation is a Lagos-based NGO, guided by a board of trustees and carried out in the community by volunteers.

Our trustees

Why we exist

Today, the Sanusi Jafar Foundation is a grassroots non-profit organisation in Lagos, committed to restoring hope, dignity and belonging for children, women, young people and vulnerable families in underserved communities.

Our work focuses on:

  • Child Welfare

    Creating experiences, support and opportunities that help children in Lagos feel seen, valued and able to dream.

  • Women Empowerment

    Supporting mothers and women across Lagos in ways that strengthen households and create greater possibilities.

  • Youth Development

    Creating opportunities for young people to develop, participate and believe in their potential.

  • Community Outreach

    Showing up where people are, responding to real needs and building stronger community connections.

But beneath everything we do is one simple philosophy:

Impact begins at the grassroots.

We don’t believe people should only be remembered when there is an event, a crisis or a festive season.

We want to build relationships with communities, listen to their realities, understand their needs and create opportunities for meaningful, lasting support. See how this approach powers our flagship outreach Christmas in the Street, as well as the verified outcomes on our Impact page.

Because helping a child is not only about the child.

The Sanusi Jafar Foundation is about more than giving.

It’s about:

  • Hope
  • Dignity
  • Belonging
  • Opportunity
  • Community

Our guiding line

When you help a child, you take a burden off a family. When you support a mother, you strengthen a household. And when you invest in a community, you create possibilities that can reach far beyond one person.

Our mission

To restore hope, dignity and belonging, one child, one family, one community at a time.

The Sanusi Jafar Foundation creates meaningful opportunities and practical support for children, women, young people and vulnerable families in underserved communities across Lagos.

Through child welfare programmes, women empowerment initiatives, youth development and community outreach, we meet immediate needs while building pathways to opportunity, connection and long-term wellbeing—in alignment with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals. Everything we do is community-led, rooted in partnerships and designed to last.

We believe impact is more than what we give.

It is how we make people feel, what possibilities we open, and what changes because we showed up.

Our vision

A future where every child feels seen, every mother feels supported, every young person sees possibility, and every community knows it matters.

We envision communities where circumstances do not define potential and where opportunity is never decided by where a person comes from. No child should feel that joy, belonging, or possibility is reserved for someone else.

As a Lagos-based NGO committed to grassroots change, we want to help build communities where people are not simply beneficiaries of support, but active partners in shaping a better future for themselves and those around them.

Because everyone deserves to feel that they belong.

Because everyone deserves to feel that they belong.

What we believe

  • 1

    Belonging matters

    Every person deserves to feel seen, valued and included.

  • 2

    Impact begins at the grassroots

    The people closest to a problem should be part of shaping its solution.

  • 3

    Small moments can create lasting memories

    A smile, an opportunity, a helping hand or simply showing up can mean more than we realise.

  • 4

    Sustainable change requires consistency

    We want to move beyond one-off interventions and build lasting relationships with communities.

  • 5

    When one person is supported, the impact can reach many

    • Help a child, strengthen a family.
    • Support a mother, empower a household.
    • Invest in a community, create possibilities for generations.
1,000smiles

Project 1,000 Smiles

From one memory to a bigger mission

Our next initiative, Project 1,000 Smiles, was born from this belief.

It represents our commitment to move beyond one-off moments of generosity and build a more consistent, year-round connection with the communities we serve in Lagos.

The goal isn’t simply to create 1,000 smiles.

It is to create 1,000 moments of hope, inclusion and possibility, while building something that can continue long after the smile fades.

Because sometimes, what looks like a small moment to us becomes a lifelong memory for someone else.

That is the kind of impact we want to create.

Discover Project 1,000 Smiles

Looking ahead

We envision a Sanusi Jafar Foundation that grows with the communities it serves.

  • A foundation that listens before it acts.
  • That measures its impact.
  • That builds partnerships around shared purpose.
  • That creates opportunities rather than dependency.
  • And that continues to remind people, especially those who may feel overlooked, that they matter.

We are not simply building programmes.

  • We are building belonging.
  • We are building relationships.
  • We are building opportunities.

And we are building a future where no child has to watch from the outside and wonder if they belong.

One child. One family. One community at a time.
